title: AXP FY2022 10-K — Table 4: Expenses Summary (p49)
key_points: AXP's expense taxonomy consists of exactly six functional categories: Card Member rewards, Business development, Card Member services, Marketing, Salaries and employee benefits, and Other, net — none of which is labeled cost of goods sold or cost of services.
Total expenses were 41,095 (2022), 33,110 (2021) and 27,061 (2020), up $7,985M or 24% year over year in 2022.

Year-over-year 2022 changes by category: Card Member rewards +$2,995M (+27%); Business development +$1,181M (+31%); Card Member services +$966M (+48%); Marketing +$167M (+3%); Salaries and employee benefits +$1,012M (+16%); Other, net +$1,664M (+35%).

Card Member rewards increase was driven by Membership Rewards and cash back rewards expenses of ~$2.0 billion plus cobrand rewards expense of ~$1.0 billion, both primarily driven by higher billed business.

Business development expense rose on increased partner payments and client incentives driven by higher network volumes; Card Member services rose on higher usage of travel-related benefits; Marketing rose on business investments to drive growth and accelerate new card acquisitions.
Other, net increased primarily due to net losses on Amex Ventures investments in the current year versus net gains in the prior year.

title: AXP FY2022 10-K — Table 2: Total Revenues Net of Interest Expense Summary (p47)
key_points: AXP's headline revenue measure is "Total revenues net of interest expense" (52,862 in 2022; 42,380 in 2021; 36,087 in 2020), i.e. revenue is presented after deducting interest expense rather than as a gross top line.

2022 revenue components and growth: Discount revenue 30,739 (+25%, +$6,176M); Net card fees 6,070 (+17%, +$875M); Service fees and other revenue 4,521 (+36%, +$1,205M); Processed revenue 1,637 (+5%, +$81M); Total non-interest revenues 42,967 (+24%).
Total interest income 12,658 (+40%); total interest expense 2,763 (variance of 100% or more); net interest income 9,895 (+28%).
Discount revenue growth was primarily driven by a 23% increase in billed business; net card fees growth was primarily driven by growth in premium card portfolios.

Service fees and other revenue growth was driven by FX-related revenues on Card Member cross-currency spending, higher travel commissions and fees, and growth in delinquency fees, partly offset by a prior-year non-cash gain related to GBTG's equity book value.

title: AXP FY2022 10-K — Consolidated Results of Operations: 2022 reporting presentation changes (p47)
key_points: Beginning Q1 2022, AXP separately presented revenues earned from processed volumes — previously reported within Discount revenue, Other fees and commissions and Other revenue — as a new line "Processed revenue".
The remaining balances of Other fees and commissions and Other revenue were combined into "Service fees and other revenue".
AXP also disaggregated the former combined "Marketing and business development" expense into two separate lines: Business development expense and Marketing expense.

Prior-period amounts in the FY2022 10-K were recast to conform to the current presentation, with no impact to Total non-interest revenues or Total expenses — so the FY2021 comparatives shown are restated, not as originally filed.
For discussion of 2021 versus 2020, the filing explicitly refers readers to the FY2021 Form 10-K filed with the SEC on February 11, 2022.
raw_excerpt: Beginning in the first quarter of 2022, we made reporting presentation changes to our Consolidated Statements of Income to separately present revenues earned from processed volumes, previously reported in Discount revenue, Other fees and commissions and Other revenue, as Processed revenue. The remaining balances from Other fees and commissions and Other revenue were combined as Service fees and other revenue. We also disaggregated Marketing and business development expense into Business Development expense and Marketing expense. Prior period amounts presented herein have been recast to conform to the current period presentation; there was no impact to Total non-interest revenues or Total expenses.

title: AXP FY2022 10-K — MD&A narrative on expense variability and marketing investment (p46)
key_points: AXP describes Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses as generally correlated to volumes or variable based on usage, rising with network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits.

Marketing is characterized as discretionary growth investment ("significant investments in marketing to drive growth momentum and accelerate new card acquisitions") rather than as a cost of delivering a product.
Operating expenses increased 24% year over year, driven by net losses on Amex Ventures equity investments versus prior-year net gains, plus higher compensation costs from an increased colleague base.
AXP frames its cost management as "driving marketing and operating expense efficiencies, while continuing to invest in our growth strategy".
raw_excerpt: Card Member rewards, Card Member services and Business development expenses are generally correlated to volumes or are variable based on usage, and increased year-over year due to network volume growth and higher usage of travel-related benefits. Card Member rewards expense growth was also driven by a larger proportion of billed business in categories that earn incremental rewards such as travel. During the year, we continued to make significant investments in marketing to drive growth momentum and accelerate new card acquisitions.

title: AXP FY2022 10-K — Revenue recognition and contra-revenue accounting policies (p102–p103)
key_points: Processed revenue represents royalties, fees and amounts earned for facilitating transactions on cards issued by network partners, recorded at the time the Card Member transaction occurs.

The issuer rate paid to network card issuing partners is recorded as contra-revenue within Processed revenue to the extent there is revenue from the same customer; any additional issuer rate is recorded as expense in Business development.

Payments made under contractual arrangements with merchants, network partners and other customers are classified as contra-revenue, except where AXP receives goods, services or other benefits with determinable and measurable fair value, in which case they are recorded as expense.

Marketing expense includes costs for development and initial placement of advertising, expensed in the period the advertising first takes place; all other marketing expenses are generally expensed as incurred.
These policies show that partner/merchant economics are netted against revenue or classified as business development expense, rather than being accumulated into a cost-of-sales line.
raw_excerpt: Our network card issuing partners receive an issuer rate that is individually negotiated between that issuer and us and is recorded as contra-revenue within Processed revenue to the extent that there is revenue from the same customer, after which any additional issuer rate is recorded as expense in Business development. ... Contra-revenue — Payments made pursuant to contractual arrangements with our merchants, network partners, and other customers are classified as contra-revenue, except where we receive goods, services or other benefits for which the fair value is determinable and measurable, in which case they are recorded as expense.

title: Boeing 2022 Form 10-K — Program accounting and gross margin usage (pp.35, 50)
key_points: Boeing uses "gross profit margin" / "combined gross margins" in the context of program accounting, meaning the estimated margin over the accounting quantity of a long-term contract, not a company-wide revenue-minus-COGS ratio.
Boeing discloses sensitivity: a ±1% change in combined gross margins on profitable long-term contracts would change 2022 pre-tax income by approximately $300 million.
Boeing states the 777X program had near break-even gross margins at December 31, 2022.

title: AXP FY2022 10-K — Business Environment (p45)
key_points: AXP reported FY2022 net income of $7.5 billion, or $9.85 per share, versus $8.1 billion, or $10.02 per share, a year earlier.

Management attributes the reduction in net income to credit reserve builds and net losses in the Amex Ventures strategic investment portfolio in 2022, versus sizeable credit reserve releases and significant net gains in that portfolio in 2021.
Provisions for credit losses increased versus the prior year, reflecting a reserve build of $617 million compared with a reserve release of $2.5 billion in the prior year.
Worldwide network volumes rose 21% (24% FX-adjusted) and billed business rose 23% (25% FX-adjusted) in 2022.
Billed business represented 86% of total network volumes and is described as the most significant driver of AXP's financial results.
U.S. Consumer billed business grew 24% and Commercial Services billed business grew 21% year over year.
International billed business grew 23% (36% FX-adjusted), driven by a strong recovery in spend across consumer and commercial customers.

T&E spending momentum remained strong throughout the year, while year-over-year Goods & Services spending growth slowed toward the end of 2022 after large pandemic-recovery growth rates earlier in the year.
Inflation was a modest contributor to billed business growth, while the strengthening U.S. dollar had a negative impact on international billings.

Total revenues net of interest expense rose 25% (27% FX-adjusted), reflecting strong growth in all revenue lines; discount revenue +25%, net card fees +17%, service fees and other revenues +36% partly on higher travel-related revenues, net interest income +28% on Card Member loan growth.
Card Member loans increased 22% year over year, with the majority of growth from existing Card Members.
Rising interest rates had a fairly neutral impact on full-year 2022 results but a modest negative impact on net interest income toward year end.

title: AXP FY2022 10-K — Provisions for Credit Losses narrative (p61)
key_points: Card Member loans and receivables provisions increased primarily due to reserve builds in 2022 versus reserve releases in 2021, plus higher net write-offs in 2022.
